Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
706 PM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Overall, the trend on the precip amounts and wind gusts is
downward. Thus, no changes to the Wind Advisory.

The Aviation discussion was updated for the 00Z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the region
through Thanksgiving Day, with frequent wind gusts strong enough to
bring down temporary outdoor structures such as tents and holiday
decorations, and produce isolated power outages. Widespread
rainfall is expected tonight, with locally heavy rain possible
mainly east of I-77, however the overall flood risk appears low.
2. Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue
through Friday. Light wintry precipitation is possible near the
Tennessee border Thursday night and Friday with no significant
accumulation. Warmer for the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: A robust low pressure system is likely to impact the
region through Thanksgiving Day, with frequent wind gusts strong
enough to bring down temporary outdoor structures such as tents and
holiday decorations, and produce isolated power outages. Widespread
rainfall is expected tonight, with locally heavy rain possible
mainly east of I-77, however the overall flood risk appears low.

The overall forecast scenario remains largely on track this
afternoon, with a strong low pressure system expected to deepen and
move northward along the Gulf Stream tonight and then northward
across central NC Thursday morning. Already we have observed
frequent wind gusts up to 40 mph from the northeast flow underneath
a cold air damming wedge firmly entrenched east of the mtns. Thus,
the wind advisory seems to be working out as designed. Note that the
Advisory does not include the mtn valleys in the TN border counties
as well as Buncombe County NC because the strong wind gusts are
expected to remain above 3500 feet in those areas. While gusts
probably won't be any stronger than 45 mph away from the highest
mountain peaks, the Advisory will remain in place because of the
potential for significant impacts. A few power outages could result
and gusts will be capable of blowing over holiday decorations,
tents, portable canopies, etc, many of which are only rated for
25 mph gusts. Be prepared for wind gusts to turn over outdoor
cooking appliances; have a fire extinguisher handy. No change to
the expiration time. As the sfc low tracks east of the Piedmont
in the morning, the pressure gradient relaxes temporarily to allow
gusts to drop off substantially. Wind will increase again, though,
Thursday afternoon.

Meanwhile, the leading edge of the precip continues to push
W/NW over the western Piedmont/Upstate into the dry air across
the foothills, and will gradually take over the region as
isentropic lift and southeast upslope flow above the wedge steadily
improve. Precip probs go categorical by midnight. Temps remain warm
enough for all rain. However, overall the QPF has dropped with this
cycle, possibly because the expected track of the low would take
the center farther to the east of the fcst area, thus we don't
get the benefit of the better low level convergence near the low
center track or the better upslope flow from the low level jet. We
remain in a Marginal Risk for excessive rain, but the likelihood
of signficant rain across our region has trended downward. Unless
the low track shifts back to the west, the flood risk appears
low. Some localized poor drainage flooding could still occur,
mainly along/E of I-77, if storm drains get clogged by leaves.


Key message 2: Gusty winds redevelop Thursday afternoon and continue
through Friday. Light wintry precipitation is possible near the
Tennessee border Thursday night and Friday with no significant
accumulation. Warmer for the weekend.

With the sfc low pulling away to the north on Thursday afternoon,
the pressure gradient will return but with southwest wind aloft that
will mix down easily underneath a subsidence inversion, though not
as strong as what we expect through tonight. Gusts are expected
to be frequent through Thursday night with strong cold advection
and should persist through Friday until sunset or thereabouts,
but the potential looks like it will top out in the 25 to 35 mph
range at best, thus sub-advisory. Unless new guidance comes in,
an extension of the current Advisory or the issuance of a new
one is not planned. As to the precip, colder air aloft associated
with the upper low moving northeast up the TN valley will allow a
changeover from rain to snow showers with the expected wrap-around
precip along the TN border Thursday evening. The movement of the
upper low, pulling out more to the north than usual, will keep
the low level flow more W or WSW, which is less-than-favorable
for upslope forcing away from parts of the Smokies, which is a
limiting factor. All together, the potential for snow accum looks
to be an inch or less near the TN border. Places east of the spine
would most likely remain dry. Temps will be cool and on the order
of ten degrees below normal on Friday, making it feel more like
a typical winter day.

The rest of the period looks relatively benign. The upper flow
goes nearly zonal across the South by Saturday with sfc high
pressure moving over the Southeast, which supports a nice warmup
back to normal. A strong shortwave is expected to move out across
the Plains Saturday night and Sunday which will develop another
strong sfc low moving northeastward across the Midwest and lower
Great Lakes Sunday into Monday morning, well to our northwest. This
system should push a cold front across our region Sunday night or
early Monday, but the front will be running out of moisture as it
moves east. While there is some potential for moisture return from
the Gulf ahead of the front, thus perhaps higher precip probs than
some of the guidance would suggest, it is likely that amounts will
be under a quarter inch across all but southwest NC. The flow goes
zonal again behind this system, so more temps near normal can be
expected from Monday onward.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Busy TAFs continue thru Thanksgiving Day. All
terminals are MVFR or lower at time of 00z TAF issuance. Expect
all sites to have IFR cigs develop overnight and possibly persist
thru the day. There were some hints that cigs could improve during
the day, but latest guidance has trended more pessimistic. In
fact, some guidance has cigs lowering to LIFR in the aftn and
continuing into the evening across the Piedmont, as a cold-air
damming wedge weakens and an inversion lowers. Confidence remains
low on what cigs will ultimately do from late morning thru late
evening Thursday. As for precip, rain has remained very light,
with only patchy MVFR vsby. At this point, not expecting vsby
to be as restrictive as the cigs. Rain should start to taper off
late morning to early aftn from south to north on Thursday. Winds
will remain gusty thru the night, but a notable lull is expected
Thursday morning, as low pressure tracks nearby. Winds will back
from NE to N, then toggle to W/SW in the 17-20z time frame. Winds
will then start to increase and become gusty by early evening
across KCLT and the Upstate sites. LLWS still remains a concern,
especially across the mountains and the NW Piedmont (impacting
KAVL and KHKY). Profiles elsewhere still show enough mixing and
deep inversion to keep bulk of the LLWS above 3000 ft AGL.

Outlook: Ceilings will improve late Thursday as drier air wraps
in behind the departing sfc low. However, a pesky stratocu deck
in the MVFR to low-VFR range may linger Thursday night and well
into Friday. Gusty west to southwest winds will also linger thru
Friday. VFR conditions should return Saturday. Then another front
may bring a brief shot at rain and restrictions late Sunday.
